concepts.why: The presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice are consistent with Tricuspid Atresia.
The presence of a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects are consistent with Ventricular Septal Defect.

The presence of cyanotic mucous membranes, a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and severe tricuspid regurgitation are consistent with Tetralogy of Fallot.

The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein producing bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels are consistent with Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
The presence of cyanotic mucous membranes, a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, and severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle are consistent with Ebstein's Anomaly.
